title: Florida House, District 34
what_it_does: Represents District 34 (Indian River, Part of Brevard) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings. Positions have not been researched yet.

candidates.name: Robert Brackett
candidates.occupation: Corporate managing partner/director; former mayor of Vero Beach; state representative (first elected 2022)
candidates.background: Brackett, a Vero Beach native and Lipscomb University graduate, served as mayor of Vero Beach before winning HD 34 in 2022. He sits on the House Select Committee on Property Taxes.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

property_tax.summary: Voted for HJR 1F to place the homestead-exemption amendment on the ballot and was recorded as a yes after the roll call on HJR 203, but told News 6 he questioned whether the amendment was the answer and stressed public safety funding.
property_tax.quote: We've got to rein it in. In 2014 we collected about $28 billion statewide in property taxes and this year we'll collect just under $60 billion.

sources.title: Floor Vote for CS/HJR 1F, Save Our Homes from Excessive Property Taxes (2026 special session), Florida House
Floor Vote for CS/CS/HJR 203, Elimination of Non-school Property Taxes for Homesteads, Florida House
2026 Voter's Guide - Florida House District 34, Republican primary (ClickOrlando / News 6)

taxes.summary: Says cutting government spending allows cutting taxes.
taxes.quote: It's pretty simple math, reduce government spending and we can reduce taxes.

sources.title: The Issues — Robert Brackett for State Representative
2026 Voter's Guide - Florida House District 34, Republican primary (ClickOrlando / News 6)

immigration.summary: Voted for SB 2-C in the February 2025 special session, which created a State Board of Immigration Enforcement, required state and local cooperation with federal immigration enforcement and added state penalties for people in the country illegally.

sources.title: Floor Vote for SB 2-C, Immigration (2025 special session), Florida House

education_choice.summary: Voted for HB 1 (2023), which opened Florida's private-school scholarship (voucher) programs to every K-12 student regardless of family income.

sources.title: Floor Vote for CS/CS/CS/CS/HB 1, Education (universal school choice), Florida House

abortion.summary: Voted for SB 300 (2023), the Heartbeat Protection Act, which bans most abortions after six weeks of pregnancy.

sources.title: Floor Vote for SB 300, Pregnancy and Parenting Support (Heartbeat Protection Act), Florida House

guns.summary: Voted for HB 543 (2023), which allowed carrying a concealed firearm without a license, and for HB 759 (2025) and HB 133 (2026), which would lower the minimum age to buy a rifle or shotgun from 21 to 18.

candidates.name: Jordyn Balderas
candidates.background: Balderas, 21, is a community organizer from Vero Beach who left high school to support his family after his mother was diagnosed with amyloidosis, and experienced homelessness as a teenager. He says he is currently uninsured and is running on housing, health care access and working-family representation.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

housing.summary: Would rehabilitate vacant properties for workforce housing, expand rental subsidies and add renter protections such as longer notice for rent increases and fee limits.

sources.title: State Representative 34 — VOTE411 Voter Guide (League of Women Voters of Florida)

education_choice.summary: Wants public dollars kept in public schools and reporting requirements for every voucher dollar.
education_choice.quote: Private for-profit schools should not piggyback off already underfunded public schools.

guns.summary: Supports stricter gun laws, including barring high-school minors from buying or carrying firearms and requiring safe storage around minors.
